transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-03-11 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
- Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Rios (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Evan Zhao (NovusCart Head of Search), Lina Morales (ML Engineer), Samir Khan (Platform)

Summary:
Redwood ran a hosted API quickstart focused on embeddings + reranking for NovusCart's product search relevance use case. Demo covered: embeddings endpoint, simple vector retrieval, Redwood hosted reranker endpoint that accepts candidates + query, console settings for batching and cache, and Optimize suggestions for cost/latency. Customer asked about latency SLOs, data residency, KMS integrations, and evidence (benchmarks). Next steps and ownership captured.

Topics:
- Current stack & pain points (existing vector DB, cost, slow rerank, holiday traffic)
- Hosted embeddings: model choices & tradeoffs
- Reranker endpoint flow: retrieve -> rerank -> serve
- Console walkthrough: throttles, prefix/KV cache, batching windows
- Security & compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope & success metrics (MRR/NDCG, p95 latency, cost per query)

Action items (quick list, more detailed in metadata):
- Redwood to send pricing and security docs, seed notebook, trial key
- NovusCart to provide sample corpus and target metrics

Transcript body:
[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Morgan from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this account — say hi diego and priya?
[00:06] Diego: hi all, diego here, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll run the demo and answer the deep tech questions, thanks for the time.
[00:11] Evan: thanks, Morgan. Quick heads up we're on a tight timeline for the spring sale, so main goals are lower p95 latencies and better top-5 relevance for commerce queries.
[00:21] Morgan: perfect, that's what we'll target. Lina, can you say a bit about your current pipeline?
[00:25] Lina: sure, we use an open-source vector store in-house, retrieval via ANN, then a BERT-based ranker running on CPU — cost and throughput are the problem, also we see lot of tail queries during promos.
[00:37] Samir: also, we need something that plugs into our VPC eventually, but for pilot we're open to hosted if data isn't persisted long-term.
[00:45] Diego: good context. Today we're going to show the hosted embeddings endpoint and a hosted reranker flow. it's designed to accept query + up to N candidates, returns a re-ordered list with scores — low integration surface.
[00:55] [01:03] Morgan: quick agenda: 1) embeddings generation and sample retrieval; 2) reranker demo with live sample; 3) console and optimize tips; 4) security and next steps.
[01:12] Diego: jumping in — i'll share my screen. (screen share) you can see the Redwood console, quick note the model catalog has curated options, for embeddings we recommend the 'redwood-emb-compact-v2' for dense product vectors or the 'redwood-embed-larger' if you need multi-lingual. (murmur) sometimes transcript shows redwood-embed as redwood-embedder, apologies.
[01:33] [02:01] Diego: here's a sample curl to the embeddings hosted endpoint — POST to /v1/embeddings with text, you get back a float32 vector by default. we also support quantized output on the host side to reduce payload.
[02:15] Lina: when you say quantized, do you store quantized vectors in the db or is that a transport compression?
[02:22] Diego: good question, currently it's transport + optional quantized payload, but common pattern is generate float vectors and down-convert for storage. we also support on-the-fly quantized inference for memory savings. (some cross-talk)
[02:36] Evan: what's typical latency for embeddings?
[02:39] Diego: for the compact model you're looking at 8-20ms per request p50 on hosted, depending on sequence length. p95 is higher, obviously, but prefix cache and batching can push effective p95 down.
[02:52] [03:10] Morgan: let's switch to rerank. Diego, run the request with our demo data.
[03:15] Diego: sure. i'm calling /v1/rerank with body { query: "waterproof hiking boots", candidates: [array of 10 items with brief text, price, id], features: optional }. you receive back a list with scores and explanations if you enable 'debug': true. (keyboard clicks)
[03:33] [04:02] System note: transcript sometimes mislabels speakers — 'Speaker 2' may show up.
[04:06] Diego: result came back p50 ~45ms for reranker alone with the 'rerank-large' profile when run in our hosted cluster. the end-to-end retrieve+rerank depends on retrieval method, but typical hosted + Redwood reranker is in the 70-200ms range for 10 candidates.
[04:22] Lina: 70-200ms is a wide range — what are levers to hit our 150ms p95 SLA?
[04:29] Diego: main levers: reduce candidate count, use smaller reranker model or quantized variant, enable KV prefix cache if queries share prefixes, and tune batching windows in the console. also dedicated capacity reduces tail variance.
[04:42] [05:00] Morgan: note that for your traffic spikes during promos, dedicated pools with burst capacity or autoscale can be more predictable — lifecycle tradeoff is cost vs. predictability.
[05:11] Evan: okay cost question — what's cost per query versus running our BERT in-house?
[05:16] Morgan: depends on query volume. rough ballpark for hosted rerank request with 10 candidates on compact model is about $0.0012 per query, but we'll send a detailed pricing sheet. dedicated committed pricing reduces unit cost.
[05:28] Samir: security: we need SOC 2, KMS, and audit logs. how does Redwood handle data retention and encryption?
[05:36] Priya: we have SOC 2 Type II, we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; hosted has encryption at rest and in transit, and we can enable request-level audit logging. i'll share our security whitepaper link.
[05:47] [06:12] Lina: for hosted pilot we want to avoid storing raw PII — can we configure ephemeral persistence or TTLs?
[06:20] Diego: yes, TTL and non-persistent caching are possible; you can also configure token-level redaction or skip logging for specific datasets. for regulated customers we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) which gives more controls and brings KMS/HSM integrations.
[06:35] Evan: any competitors mentioned while evaluating? we've looked at Pinecone + separate model host, also considered OpenAI endpoints but worried about cost and lack of on-prem options.
[06:47] Morgan: that's common. Redwood's differentiator is the unified runtime + routing — same API across hosted/dedicated/private, plus Optimize suggestions to tune batch/caching.
[06:59] [07:30] Diego: switching to the console — here's the Optimize tab that surfaces batching suggestions, model quantization recommendations, and sample cost impact. for example, changing batching window from 10ms to 30ms increased throughput 2x in our internal tests but added about 10ms median latency.
[07:50] Lina: can Optimize export suggested configs as terraform or as a config blob?
[07:54] Diego: currently you can export as JSON config and we have an open-source terraform provider in our repo — i'll link it. small mis-remembering: names in the console sometimes show 'Optimize' as 'Optimizer' in older builds, apologies.
[08:10] [09:00] Morgan: let's do a live A/B: rerank-large vs rerank-compact on your sample query set — i'll hand control to diego.
[09:07] Diego: running batch of 200 sample queries from our demo set; comparing NDCG@5 and p95 latency. (typing) initial results: compact has +0.6% lower NDCG but halves median latency. for many commerce use cases that's acceptable tradeoff.
[09:27] Evan: the NDCG delta is small, but how about edge cases like product attribute matches and sponsored items?
[09:33] Diego: we can add lightweight features into reranker payload like price, recency, and boost flags. reranker accepts arbitrary candidate features in the payload for feature cross. note: feature serialization sometimes appears weird in the transcript as 'feecher' but it's just JSON.
[09:52] [11:00] Samir: we need an end-to-end integration plan — we're on Kubernetes, infra team prefers minimal vendor-side egress to our DB. how does integration look?
[11:09] Morgan: for pilot you can keep DB in your environment, call our embeddings endpoint to compute vectors (or compute locally and upload), then have retrieval in your infra and call Redwood reranker with candidate list. for production you can move retrieval to a managed vector store or keep it in-house and use Redwood only for rerank.
[11:27] Lina: data residency — do you have EU region hosting? some catalogs are EU-only.
[11:31] Priya: yes, we have hosted regions in us-east, eu-west, and ap-southeast; for strict residency customers we recommend Redwood Private in-region.
[11:41] [12:30] Diego: demo note — i'll create a simple notebook gist that does: 1) call embeddings, 2) upsert into example ANN (we use faiss in the notebook), 3) run retrieval locally for candidates, 4) call rerank endpoint with candidates, 5) compute offline metrics. that should be easy to drop into your CI.
[12:49] Evan: great. about SLAs, what's uptime and latency guarantees for hosted?
[12:54] Morgan: hosted has a best-effort SLA for free tiers; enterprise hosted commitments and Dedicated plans come with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. we'll include numbers in the follow-up doc.
[13:06] [13:30] Lina: curious about model drift and eval — does Redwood provide continuous quality monitoring?
[13:35] Diego: yes, Redwood Optimize can run periodic evals on a holdout prompt set and alert on regressions in NDCG or average relevance. you can upload labeled prompts and set thresholds.
[13:48] Evan: can we run a short benchmark with our 500 queries? we'd like to see before/after A/B and cost math.
[13:55] Morgan: absolutely — next steps we'll provision trial keys, drop the notebook, and run a small benchmark. Diego will coordinate.
[14:04] [14:30] Priya: i'll attach our SOC2 and KMS docs to the follow-up email. Morgan will send pricing and pilot contract template.
[14:37] Samir: one more thing — what about caching similarity across queries? we have many near-duplicate searches.
[14:43] Diego: prefix/KV cache can dedupe expensive KV cache hits by key and preserve KV across requests; it's useful when customers have repeat queries. You can also enable snippet-level caching in the routing layer. sometimes the console shows it as 'KV cash' in logs, small transcribe quirk.
[14:59] [16:00] Morgan: wrapping up — recap: 1) Redwood to provide trial API key, pricing & security docs; 2) Diego to send reranker notebook + terraform config; 3) NovusCart to share 500-query sample and a small corpus. success metrics: NDCG uplift > 1.5% and p95 latency < 150ms.
[16:25] Evan: sounds good, thanks everyone. If we hit those numbers we'll look at dedicated capacity for peak windows.
[16:32] Morgan: thanks, we'll follow up by end of day with materials.
[16:37] (call ends)
